subject: Clarify invoice line items & commit discounts for BlueWave
content:
From: Sasha Trent <sasha.trent@bluewave.ai>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Question on commits, discounts, and invoice detail

Hi Karthik —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Before we move to an internal approval, procurement has two accounting questions I need to surface:

1) Commit tiers — you mentioned monthly commit tiers with blended per-token pricing. Can you confirm whether the per-token discount is applied retroactively for the whole month once we hit a tier, or if it only applies prospectively from the point the tier is met?

2) Invoice line items — finance requires the invoice to show a token-level breakdown: raw tokens consumed per model, committed vs overage charges, and discounts applied. Do you provide an export we can ingest into our billing system?

3) Export format — ideally CSV with columns: date, model, tokens_prompt, tokens_completion, total_tokens, committed_tokens_applied, discount_rate, net_charge. Can you supply a sample?

We want to avoid surprises on the first invoice. Brad (cc) is our finance lead; procurement@bluewave.ai is on the loop.

Appreciate a quick note so I can put this into the MA-Plan doc.

— Sasha
Senior Sourcing Manager
BlueWave Analytics

---

On Thu, 26 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -0800, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai wrote:
To: Sasha Trent <sasha.trent@bluewave.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rachel_kim@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Question on commits, discounts, and invoice detail

Hi Sasha — great questions, and thanks for looping finance. High level answers up front, then specifics and attachments.

1) Retroactive vs prospective: our hosted commitments are billed on a monthly cadence. Discounts are applied retroactively for the billing period — meaning if your aggregate monthly usage crosses a higher tier, the effective per-token price for that billing month will be calculated at the tiered rate and shown as an adjustment on the invoice (we show both gross and net lines). Practically this results in a credit on the invoice if the higher tier triggers a lower effective price than what was charged at time-of-request.

2) Invoice line items & export: yes, we provide a usage export and an invoice CSV that mirrors what is on the invoice. The export includes per-request token counts aggregated by model, date, and route. We also include a reconciliation section that maps committed tokens vs overage and the computed discount.

3) Sample attached: I attached sample_usage_export.csv (redacted) and a short commit_summary.pdf that shows the calculation logic and how credits appear on month-end invoices.

Quick notes:
- Committed capacity (monthly) is treated as a pool of tokens for the billing month. Any consumption beyond the pool is billed at the published overage rate for the tier.
- Discounts are tiered: e.g., 0–500M tokens = list price; 500M–2B = 8% discount; >2B = 15% discount (this is illustrative; we will lock exact bands in the SOW).
- For accounting, the invoice will include three lines per billed model: gross_charge, discount_credit, net_charge. We can also export a line-level CSV that includes the discount_rate applied per aggregation row.

Rachel / Marissa — looping you in for confirmation on the invoice CSV columns and whether we need any special ledger codes for BlueWave.

Action items:
- Sasha: confirm the CSV column template in your message is sufficient or add additional fields.
- Us: provide a sample invoice export and draft amendment with explicit commit bands.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Sasha —

Thanks for raising these—this is exactly the level of detail procurement needs. Attached is a short sample_usage_export.csv with the columns you requested and a small reconciliation table that mirrors how we surface the three-line invoice for each model. A few clarifying points for your finance team:

- The CSV includes both prompt and completion token counts per aggregation bucket (we aggregate hourly by model by default, but we can provide daily aggregation if you prefer).
- committed_tokens_applied in the CSV will show how much of the committed pool was applied to each aggregation row (this is helpful for line-level reconciliation).
- The discount_rate column will show the effective discount applied for that billing month after retroactive calculation.
- If you require cost center or GL codes on the invoice lines, send over the mapping file and we can surface that in a separate invoice supplement (PDF).

I attached a proposed_amendment.docx that includes the concrete commit bands (draft). Karthik — please review the bands (500M/2B/5B) and the overage rates in section 2 before we send to the customer.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Billing & Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference
